name: obstack-js
description: obstack SDK for Node.js — OTel setup, LLM auto-instrumentation and agent/tool spans in two lines
//dependencies: Every runtime dep is load-bearing for the two-line setup (S2.1 L1 wants the reason stated, so it is stated here rather than in a commit message that nobody reads again). api: the tracer/context calls in traceAgent/traceTool and both instrumentations. sdk-node: the NodeSDK init() assembles (D78). sdk-trace: BatchSpanProcessor plus the SpanProcessor/ReadableSpan types the Vercel-AI translation is written against — this package rather than sdk-trace-base because sdk-node's own config type is declared against it. sdk-logs: BatchLogRecordProcessor for the log pipeline (D84 — registration only, no logging bridge). exporter-trace-otlp-proto / exporter-logs-otlp-proto: the OTLP proto-over-HTTP exporters D78 names, constructed with no args so all config stays standard OTEL_* env. instrumentation: InstrumentationBase and the require-in-the-middle module definitions the openai/anthropic patches are built on. instrumentation-http: a HARD dep on purpose (D77(c)) — it is what makes the api layer of the four-layer trace appear without the app writing a line of OTel.
//peerDependencies: The instrumented libraries are never dependencies (D77): obstack-js patches them if the app has them and does nothing at all if it does not. Optional peers say that in package metadata instead of only in prose. Every bound below is a measurement, not a guess — see README's 'What is actually covered'. openai >=4.85 <8: `openai/resources/chat/completions/completions.js` is the module whose Completions.prototype the client really uses, checked on 4.85.4 / 5.23.2 / 6.49.0 / 7.4.0. The floor is 4.85 rather than 4 because that module does not exist below it (openai kept chat completions in a flat `resources/chat/completions.js` through 4.84.1) — measured, the same call on 4.84.1 produces no span at all and no error, so a wider range would advertise coverage that silently is not there. The Responses API shares that range with a floor of its own inside it: `openai/resources/responses/responses.js` first appears in 4.87.0 — checked on 4.87.0 / 4.87.4 / 5.23.2 / 6.49.0 / 7.4.0 / 7.8.0, where the client dispatches through the `Responses.prototype.create` this SDK patches, and absent on 4.85.4 / 4.86.0 / 4.86.2, where `client.responses` is undefined and there is no Responses call to instrument — so the peer floor stays 4.85, where chat coverage is real, and the README's coverage table carries the 4.87 Responses floor rather than the package advertising a range narrower than it covers. Responses coverage is now proven at unit level on TWO of those versions in one suite (`src/instrumentation/responses.test.ts`): 4.87.0, the floor, and 7.8.0, the current release. That is not belt and braces. The Responses patch has to read the HTTP response body without consuming the one the application reads, and the shape it reads through changed inside this range: from 7.5.0 the client installs a per-instance `_thenUnwrap` (`client.js:508`) that closes over a module-local parse, so a fix measured only on 7.4.0 was a silent no-op on the current release, inside the advertised range, with CI green. A range this package advertises for a mechanism this version-sensitive is only honest if both ends of it are driven by a real client, so both are. @anthropic-ai/sdk >=0.50 <1: `resources/messages/messages.js` exists from 0.50 (0.30.1 has no such path), checked on 0.50.4 / 0.70.1 / 0.100.1 / 0.117.1. ai >=5 <8: 5.0.237 and 6.0.256 emit the ai.generateText.doGenerate OTel span this SDK translates (src/vercel-ai.ts); 7.x emits no OTel span at all — it moved telemetry to a public integration registry, which is the door the v7 leg uses instead (src/vercel-ai-v7.ts). The upper bound moved to <8 because the 7 floor turned out to be the first 7 there is. Bisected across the published 7.0.x line — 80 versions, 19 exercised (7.0.0, .1, .5, .11, .21, .23, .25, .31, .42, .51, .52, .54, .61, .66, .71, .73, .79, .82, .85), each with a real generateText against a stub LanguageModelV4 — against the four predicates the v7 leg actually depends on: the integrations array is read at dispatch, executeLanguageModelCall wraps doGenerate and carries a callId, onStart carries operationId and the SAME callId, and the resolved result carries usage.inputTokens.total, usage.outputTokens.total, finishReason.unified, content[] and response.modelId. All four hold on all nineteen, 7.0.0 included, and none diverged — so there is no dead sub-range for the range to route around, and `>=5 <8` advertises nothing that is not there. One version-level caveat that is NOT a range bound: ai 7 declares engines.node >=22 (ai/package.json:75). obstack-js keeps engines.node >=20, because the 5/6 line runs there and raising the floor would drop apps this SDK still covers; an app on node 20 simply cannot install ai 7 in the first place, and npm says so at install time rather than at runtime.
//devDependencies: tsx/typescript/@types/node are the repo's existing runner and compiler, at apps/web's ranges so the lockfile dedupes onto the versions already there rather than resolving new ones. The three provider libraries are installed here because the unit suite drives the REAL clients against a local fake — an instrumentation test that never loads the library it patches proves nothing (S2.0 L1). context-async-hooks is test-only: the unit harness builds a bare TracerProvider, and without a context manager a span started inside another has no parent, so the nesting the four-layer trace depends on could not be asserted. Real applications get it from NodeSDK, which is why it is not a runtime dependency. It is already in the lockfile as a transitive dependency of sdk-node, so naming it here adds no resolution. ai7 is an npm alias — `npm:ai@7.0.85` — and the first alias in this repo (openai487 below is the second), so it is worth saying why one exists at all: the v5/6 leg translates spans `ai` emits and the v7 leg answers callbacks `ai` invokes, and neither test proves anything unless it runs against the real library. The two majors cannot both be `ai`, and running them in separate processes would leave the thing most worth proving unproven — that both legs are live in ONE process (which is what init() does) and still produce exactly one llm span per call. The alias pins exact, not a range: the whole point is that the suite reports which version it measured. openai487 is the second alias, `npm:openai@4.87.0`, and it exists for the same reason with a sharper edge: openai is a devDependency at `^7.8.0` because 7.8.0 is what an application installing this SDK today actually gets, and the Responses body-read mechanism differs between the pre-7.5 shape and the 7.5+ one (a per-instance `_thenUnwrap` that bypasses the promise's own parse memo), so a suite pinned to one of them cannot see a break in the other — which is exactly how one shipped. The two ends of the Responses range are therefore both driven by a real client in one suite. One wrinkle worth knowing before editing that test: require-in-the-middle derives the module name from the PATH, so nothing under `node_modules/openai487/` is ever matched by a definition named `openai`; the test copies the resolved alias once into `node_modules/.obstack-openai487/node_modules/openai` so the matcher sees the name it reads. Third version, third place: the compose sample (`demo/sdk-sample-ts`) stays pinned exact at `openai 7.4.0` per D76, so between the sample and this package the covered range is exercised at 4.87.0, 7.4.0 and 7.8.0.
